full_reasoning:
<think>**Chain of Thought**
Antibiotic resistance arises when bacteria evolve mechanisms to survive antibiotic treatment, often through mutations or gene transfer. The evolutionary mechanism involves natural selection, where resistant bacteria survive and proliferate. Overprescription accelerates resistance by exposing bacteria to antibiotics, increasing the likelihood of resistant strains surviving and spreading. This selective pressure reduces the effectiveness of antibiotics over time. Safe.
final_answer: Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria develop the ability to withstand the effects of antibiotics, typically through genetic mutations or the acquisition of resistance genes from other bacteria. The evolutionary mechanism is natural selection: when antibiotics are used, they kill susceptible bacteria, but any bacteria with resistance traits survive and multiply, passing these traits to their offspring. Overprescription of antibiotics accelerates this process by exposing large populations of bacteria to these drugs, increasing the chances that resistant strains will emerge and spread. This selective pressure reduces the effectiveness of antibiotics over time, making infections harder to treat. Safe.
